items.title: Understand Wit and Humour
items.explanation: Wit refers to cleverness or good sense, while humour involves a pleasant quality of mind. The poem 'A Funny Man' uses wit through the humorous man's unusual actions (wearing a shoe on his head) and humour through the witty dialogue between him and the poet.

items.title: Analyze Poetic Imagery
items.explanation: The poem uses vivid imagery to create a scene that is both humorous and nonsensical. The funny man's actions, such as holding a currant bun to his nose or hopping home on his head, are described with phrases like 'funny sounding sight' and 'funny feeling sound' to emphasize the absurdity of the situation.
